rationale: Registered the successor execution for the strongest remaining boundary: the harness adds a split_configurations case where a three-voter committed configuration is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted and made three voters again, the leader is partitioned from the other two in both directions and taken down, only it is restarted (with a fresh instance beside it), and both sides then run. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled both sides elected leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums — the restarted side on a one-voter reconstruction, the other two on the committed three-voter configuration — both committed an entry, and neither side held the other's entry; with the flag disabled only the two-peer side led and the restarted side refused with "node is not the leader".

scope.description: Whether a reconstruction-governed leader and the peers of the committed configuration can both lead and commit when a partition separates them. Twenty-one in-process cases: the nineteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a split_configurations case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, the leader is disconnected from the other two in both directions and stopped, only it is restarted together with a fresh empty instance, and both sides are left to elect and commit.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the partition is made with the transport's own Disconnect on both sides, and the fresh instance is connected only to the restarted leader.

The restarted leader's reconstruction is the single-voter configuration recorded by its own snapshot while the configuration entry in its log names three voters; the two partitioned peers keep the committed configuration.
Each side is given up to 800 ms to elect, then both are asked to commit one uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, and each side's log store is searched for the other side's entry afterwards.
No instance is restarted after the partition, and no other membership change is issued on the second side.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, healing of the partition, multiple sequential client changes, and any claim about what the cluster would do if the partition were repaired.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back, applies ten more entries and reads the last configuration entry into a split_inputs CA_EVENT. It disconnects the leader from both peers in both directions with the transport's Disconnect, stops the leader, restarts it over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance (own stores and FSM) connected only to it, and waits for it to lead. It then issues AddVoter for the fresh instance, waits for a leader among the two partitioned peers, records both sides' terms and reconstructed voter counts, has both sides commit a uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, waits, searches each side's log store for the other side's entry, and emits a split_result CA_EVENT with both sides' leadership, terms, voter counts, commit outcomes, whether each side holds its own and the other's entry, the derived cross_entries_seen and whether both sides lead and in the same term.
experiment.responsibility: Election quorums and leader commitments are computed from each node's own reconstructed configuration, so whether two quorums overlap is decided by that configuration rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Partition case with the flag enabled: a cluster is not expected to have a leader on the restarted side and a leader among the peers of the committed configuration at the same time.
Partition case with the flag enabled: two leaders are not expected to hold the same term.
Partition case with the flag enabled: an entry committed on one side is expected to be visible to the other side's store, so both committed entries should be found across the two sides.
Control: with the flag disabled the restarted side cannot lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable, so only the other side leads.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the split_configurations case with its flag-disabled control: the peers of the committed configuration are disconnected from the leader in both directions before it is taken down, the leader is restarted with a fresh instance beside it, and both sides are then allowed to elect, commit and be searched for each other's entry. Replaces the comparison set with the two-leader predicate, the same-term predicate, the cross-side visibility predicate and the control.
